task: Spike: compile CodeMie CLI into a self-contained pkg binary, bundle as Tauri externalBin sidecar, and validate codemie --version and codemie install [agent] on a clean macOS aarch64 VM

key_reasoning.reason: Four components across three layers: pathman.rs (Rust PATH injection — shared startup utility), lib.rs (startup hook call site), handlers.js (JS orchestration — short-circuit steps 1.2 Node check and 1.3 npm install), and a new tauri.macos.conf.json override (externalBin + signingIdentity). The previous spike documented all four touch points; the pkg approach replaces the bundle.resources JS tree with a single binary, simplifying pathman.rs detection (no symlink workaround needed).

Highest-risk unknown: @yao-pkg/pkg cannot bundle keytar.node statically — it must be declared as an asset and extracted to a temp directory at runtime. On macOS with hardened runtime, the extracted unsigned .node file may be blocked by library validation. The closest existing pattern (spike/epmcdme-14504-bundle-node externalBin mechanism) validates Tauri sidecar wiring but does not cover pkg compilation with native addons. The pkg-compiled Mach-O must also survive codesign --options runtime re-signing; if keytar is loaded unconditionally at startup, pkg compilation fails entirely. @yao-pkg/pkg is entirely new to this repo with no established pattern or guide coverage. Security/Compliance red flag applied: notarization compliance is an explicit acceptance criterion. Technical Risk bumped from XL (5) to XXL (6).

red_flags_applied: Security or Compliance requirements: Technical Risk bumped from XL (5) to XXL (6) — pkg-compiled Mach-O binary must survive codesign re-signing with --options runtime and pass notarization; unsigned extracted keytar.node may trigger macOS library validation; notarization on a clean aarch64 VM is an explicit acceptance criterion
